sources.instrument: NIST IR 8596, Cybersecurity Framework Profile for Artificial Intelligence (Cyber AI Profile): NIST Community Profile
sources.version: INITIAL PRELIMINARY DRAFT, 16 Dec. 2025 — not a final. The dataset records this as sourceStatus and the SKILL discloses it.
sources.intervalBecause: Already 180 before RW-1.13 existed, with no reason recorded — the rule found it on its first run, which is the argument for the rule. The cadence is right and now says so: the Cyber AI Profile is the newest instrument in this manifest and the only one still moving on the timescale of a release rather than a rulemaking, so a year between reads would routinely be a year out of date.

sources.label: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A identifiers (crosswalk target)
sources.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control identifiers, as referenced by NIST's CSF 2.0 Reference Export
sources.version: Crosswalk built from tools/csf-2.0.xlsx, sha256 cc4ec545…f9b616, matching the sha recorded in nist-csf-2.0-core.json. 119 identifiers, 91 referenced by NIST's export; labels are CAC paraphrases and control `text` is null — no ISO/IEC text is reproduced.

citationAllowlist.reason: Named once in SKILL.md as a crosswalk target a reader may hold, alongside ISO 27001 and CIS. CAC has no ISO licence, so no ISO/IEC text can be read or reproduced and a verified row would be a claim nobody checked. The 27001 row records the same constraint: identifiers only, labels paraphrased, control text null. Permanent, not pending.
